newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle slow in limited test-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle slow in limited test-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales were slow in a limited test, feedlot sources said.

About 1,500 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 1,000 sold in Kansas at $66.00 per cwt, but at lower quality than the bulk of sales on Tuesday at $67.00, several feedlot managers said.
"Most that's left is kind've clean-up trade and anybody that still has good cattle can still get $67.00," one Kansas feedlot manager said.
A number of feedlots reported selling out their showlists on Tuesday at $67.00.
Many cattle left unsold this week were "green" or unfinished, a Panhandle feedlot manager said.
"People are working real hard at keeping current," he said.
Activity was slowing down heading into this weekend's three day Memorial Day holiday. Nearly all meat packers will be closed on Monday in observance of the holiday.
Fed cattle prices next week could be weak, with packers seen having adequate live inventory during the short slaughter week, market sources said.
